data.title: Twin Disc Increases Quarterly Cash Dividend 25% to $0.05 Per Share
data.description: In Milwaukee on August 7, 2026, Twin Disc, Inc. revealed its latest financial move as the Board of Directors sanctioned a rise in the regular quarterly cash dividend. The dividend amount has been increased by $0.01 from the previous quarter, marking a significant surge of 25%. This brings the new cash dividend per share to $0.05. Shareholders can anticipate this dividend on September 1, 2026, provided they are recorded as shareholders at the end of business on August 18, 2026.

data.title: Employers hesitate to hire as job market trends down due to rising prices and business uncertainty, despite no layoffs.
data.description: After a brief increase in spring, business activity slowed down as summer approached, leading to a rise in prices and increased uncertainty. Fortunately, businesses were able to maintain their workforce without any layoffs during this challenging period.

data.title: Newly elected Pope Leo XIV, a Chicago native, brings hope to struggling White Sox with his timely support.
data.description: Pope Leo XIV, a native of Chicago, was recently elevated and is a lifelong supporter of the White Sox. His elevation was a significant development for the team, which has been struggling both on the field and in terms of fan support.

data.title: Promising heart drug targeting inflammation fails, casting doubt on theory that inflammation causes heart disease.
data.description: After treating thousands of patients with a drug aimed at reducing inflammation, the unexpected setback has led experts to reevaluate its effectiveness in preventing heart disease. The drug, which was specifically designed to target inflammation, demonstrated disappointing results, prompting speculation on the true role of inflammation in causing heart disease. This development has sparked debate among experts and raised doubts about the previously established link between inflammation and heart disease.

data.title: Villa Marconi Engaged in Union Busting as Agency Staff Are Hired to Fill Union Positions
data.description: In Ottawa, the union representing employees at Villa Marconi has accused the employer of engaging in union busting tactics. Agency staff were found to be replacing union members who were laid off, specifically in the laundry department where employees were unexpectedly let go in June. This has resulted in a shortage of staff and resources in the department.
